summary: End-to-end verification of FOODbakēd reusable Menu Item CRUD + new Restaurant Partner Portal. Ran the pre-existing pytest suite (9/9 pass) and drove the full UI flow via Playwright: super-admin login → restaurants list (Menu + Partners action icons render for burger_hub_ci) → PartnersModal (create partner, toggle Actif on/off, password reset, delete via API afterwards) → admin MenuManager full lifecycle (add section → add item with popular tag → variant → addon → reverse-delete) → partner portal login → dashboard tiles + toggle open/close (Statut updates Ouvert→Fermé) + prep_time_min blur update (tile reflects 25) + cover-photo present + NO Partners tab / no restaurants list → open menu manager (all 4 seed sections visible) → full add-section+item+variant+addon lifecycle as partner → dashboard restore → logout (redirects to /partner/food/login) → security (logged-out /partner/food and /partner/food/menu both redirect to /partner/food/login). Backend + Frontend integration are working end-to-end.

issues: React console warning: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' hydration error emitted inside a <select> inside item/variant modals (does not block flow, but should be cleaned up).
Console spam: 'An empty string ("") was passed to the src attribute' when an item/section has no image_url — pass null or omit src instead of empty string in FoodImageUploader / thumbnails.

Fix hydration warning: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' inside a <select> in MenuManager section-select (item modal).

critical_code_review_comments: MenuManager <option> children contain <span>, causing React hydration warnings — replace inner markup with a plain string label or use custom dropdown.
FoodImageUploader passes src="" when no image is set; guard with `{url ? : null}` to silence browser warnings.

Partner create endpoint returns a plain 'id' field; consider not accepting a caller-supplied 'id' silently (currently server generates its own even when body includes id — behavior is safe but silent).

rca of the issue: No product issues. One test-harness quirk: my initial JS-based section-id resolver walked up 8 parents from an <edit> button and matched the FIRST ancestor whose textContent contained the new section's tag, which for the QA test section ended up matching the top-level menu container that also contained the Entrées section — so the wrong sid was picked and Entrées got deleted at cleanup. Mitigated in later scripts by using a nearest-depth match strategy. Restored data via admin API.
